2  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
A memo is filed for withdrawal of compromise petition filed on 17.11.2023 as fresh compromise petition is filed.
Petitioners have no objection.
Memo is accepted.
Compromise petition filed on 17.11.2023 is dismissed as withdrawn.
Counsel for petitioners has filed application for amendment of writ petition seeking for addition of pleading and prayer.
Application is not opposed.
Being satisfied with cause shown, application is allowed.
Amended writ petition incorporating amendment is filed today, which is taken on record.
Counsel for petitioners and respondent no.4 submit that petitioners and respondent no.4 have entered into compromise.

Terms of conditions of which read as under:
NC: 2023:KHC:44554 "i) That petitioners and respondent no.4 have amicably settled right over land bearing survey no.481 measuring 2 acres 12 guntas situated at Chelur village, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagar District as per aid and advise of elders and well wishers.
ii) That now, respondents no.1 and 2 have determined compensation amount for said land in question as per General Award dated 05.07.2021 in no.KIADB-LAQ- 350/2021-22 as per Annexure-Q.

If consent award to be determined at rate of triple amount now determined, then said amount to be Rs.4,69,20,000/- out of which petitioner no.1-Rs. 75,00,000/-(16%) petitioner no.2-Rs.
Sri Chowdaiah vs The Managing Director on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142809158/
3 75,00,000/-(16%) petitioner no.4-Rs.3,19,20,000/-(68%) Total Rs.4,69,20,000/-
vi) That respondents no.1 and 2 may be directed to take steps to disburse award amount deposited and to pass consent award under Section 29(2) of KIADB Act, 1956 forthwith.
NC: 2023:KHC:44554 vii) That respondent no.4 has agreed and consented to withdraw W.P.no.10416/2022 filed against petitioners.
viii) That parties have entered into this compromise without any coercion, undue influence, force and threat."
Said compromise petition is signed by parties who are present before Court and are identified by their respective counsels.

On interaction, they have stated that terms of compromise have explained to them and that they have executed compromise after understanding same, out of their own volition without any threat, coercion or inducement or force from anyone.

Consequently direct respondents no.1 and 2 to consider request of petitioners for passing Consent Award under Section 29(2) of KIADB Act, 1966 to enable NC: 2023:KHC:44554 parties to receive amount in deposit as well as future enhanced amount to be determined with equal and proportionate shares @
50% each between petitioners and respondent no.4 as per compromise petition.

From above, it is seen that writ petition is filed challenging Annexure-V dated 02.02.2022, which is an Intimation Letter informing petitioners stating that General Award in respect of acquisition of Sri Chowdaiah vs The Managing Director on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142809158/
4 land bearing Sy.no.481 of Cheelur Village Maralavadi Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk Ramanagar District to extent of 2 Acres 12 guntas was passed and approved and that compensation amount in terms will be deposited before Court; also challenging General Award at Annexure-Q on ground that petitioners were not afforded opportunity of availing compensation under Consent Award which would be higher than General Award, on account of dispute between petitioners and respondent no.4.

It was submitted that since dispute between petitioners and respondent no.4 had been settled in view of compromise NC: 2023:KHC:44554 petition, respondent no.2 was not justified in passing General Award, denying compensation to petitioners and respondent no.4 under Consent Award.

4. In view of fact that compensation under Consent Award is considerably higher and denial of same to petitioners and respondent no.4 on ground of dispute, which has settled, would not be appropriate.
Therefore, General Award dated 05.07.2021 at Annexure-Q stands quashed insofar as land bearing Sy.no.481 measuring 2 acres 12 guntas of Maralavadi Village.
Respondent no.2 to consider petitioners' case for passing of Consent Award and thereafter SLAO shall take note of compromise petition for disbursal of amount.
Time limit for taking above steps shall be two months from date of receipt of certified copy of this Order.
Compromise petition is taken on record and accepted.
In terms of above, writ petition stands disposed of.
